quests.title: Know the Wheel
quests.description:
Stop there. You're new, and new ones walk into the Canal.

Deathguard Halloran. I hold this post and I have held it a long time, and in that time I have watched a hundred of you go over the rail.

Not from despair. From confusion.

They come up out of whatever they came up out of, they get turned around in the rotunda, and they walk very confidently into the water because every direction down here looks like the one they meant.

So before anything else: learn the wheel.

Four quarters, one wheel. Royal to the north-west. Magic north-east. War south-west. Apothecarium south-east.

Walk all four.

And learn it before it learns you - because this city does get used to people, and the ones it gets used to stop being asked where they're going.
quests.accept_text: The four great halls - Royal, Magic, War, Apothecarium. Walk them all.
quests.turn_in_text:
You came back. And you are not green.

The Undercity has a use for you yet, and that's more than it decides about most.

quests.title: A Slip for the Executor
quests.description:
Now something small, and I'd like it done properly rather than quickly.

This is a muster slip for Executor Wrenfall. She holds the Royal Quarter's north gate.

I can't leave this post. That isn't an excuse - it's the actual constraint of the job, and it's why a man who could walk this in four minutes is handing it to a stranger.

Two things.

Don't read it. Not because it's secret - I wrote it, there's nothing in it. Because the Executor is touchy about her paperwork, and she can tell, and I have watched her tell.

And put it in her hand. Not on the desk. Not with a clerk.

She's particular about that too, and after eleven years of dealing with her I've stopped asking why and started just doing it.

North promenade, west of the elevator.

objectives.label: Take Halloran's muster slip to Executor Wrenfall

quests.accept_text: The north promenade, west of the elevator. Into her hand.
quests.turn_in_text:
Halloran. Of course.

Never a word wasted, that one. Eleven years and I've not had a sentence off him I didn't need.

Here, take something for your troubles.

on_accept.name: Halloran's Muster Slip
on_accept.description: A neatly-folded slip stamped with the Deathguard sigil.

quests.title: The Crusade at the Door
quests.description:
Executor Wrenfall. Good - you can walk and you can follow an instruction. That puts you ahead.

Scarlet Zealots and Bowmen are patrolling the Tirisfal road to the Ruins.

Close enough to see the portal. I want that understood precisely, because it's the whole of the problem: they are not near our door, they are near enough to LOOK at our door, and there is a difference and it lasts about a week.

They haven't tried the gate.

I have no intention of finding out whether they're brave enough to.

That's not caution. It's that the answer is unrecoverable either way - if they try it and fail we have a siege, and if they try it and succeed we have considerably less than that.

The Scarlet Watch Post, east of Brill.

Thin them out before they find out for me. Leave none of them in sight of that road.
quests.accept_text: The Scarlet Watch Post, east of Brill.
quests.turn_in_text:
Good. The portal stays dark and the Crusade stays outside.

The quartermaster's thanks - and mine, which are worth less and cost me more.

quests.title: Orders in Scarlet Ink
quests.description:
Now I want to read what they've been told.

Not what they believe. What they've been TOLD - and the two are usually different documents, which is the single most useful thing I know about the Crusade.

Their converts and initiates carry orders. A neat red hand, every one.

And they carry them openly, which tells you something on its own: an order you carry openly is an order you've been told is righteous.

I want a handful.

A single order is a task. A row of them laid side by side is a doctrine, and I can work out what they're afraid of from a doctrine in an afternoon.

The Crusader's Outpost east of Brill, and the farm roads.

Anyone in Scarlet who can read. That narrows it considerably and I'd not have said so five years ago.
quests.accept_text: Off the Scarlet converts and initiates - the outpost east of Brill and the farm roads.
quests.turn_in_text:
A very tidy hand.

They are afraid of us. And they have been told to hide it, in writing, by somebody who thought that would help.

I find that touching.

quests.title: Tin for the Forge
quests.description:
Smith Ironbrow. Mind where you put your hands, most of this is colder than it looks and the rest isn't.

I have a bench. I have a quench trough. I have thirty years of knowing what to do with both.

I have no tin.

And the forge in the War Quarter is cold, which is the part that genuinely offends me - not that it's unsupplied, that nobody has bothered to LIGHT it. It's been sitting there dark for months because lighting it is somebody's job and nobody is sure whose.

So: smelt three tin bars at it.

That's the whole task and I know how it sounds.

Here's what it actually is. A forge that's been lit is a forge somebody is using, and a forge somebody is using gets supplied. I've been trying to get that fire started for a season by asking.

Light it and it's yours. Tin ore out of the western hills if you've no stock.

objectives.label: Smelt tin bars at the Undercity Forge

quests.accept_text: The Undercity Forge, south-west of the War Hall. Light it and smelt three bars.
quests.turn_in_text:
Three bars, and not a cinder wasted.

That's how you light a forge.

It'll be warm tomorrow. It has not been warm tomorrow in a long while.

quests.title: Iron for the Guard
quests.description:
Fire's lit, so now we make something that matters.

Rough iron. For the Royal Guard's greaves.

And before you tell me rough iron is poor stuff for a royal anything - it is, and it's what they'll get, and they'll be better off for it.

Good steel on a guard who stands at a gate all year is a waste. It wants maintaining, it wants a smith who knows it, and the moment it's scratched somebody above him decides it reflects badly.

Rough iron you can beat flat with a stone and put back on.

That's the whole philosophy and thirty years hasn't shaken it.

Three bars at the forge.

And you can use my good tongs, which I don't offer.

Don't touch the ones on the left. They bite. I'm not going to explain how.

objectives.label: Smelt rough iron bars at the Undercity Forge

quests.accept_text: Three rough iron bars at the Undercity Forge.
quests.turn_in_text:
Rough iron, rough work.

The Guard will wear them with pride. Or at least with plates, which lasts longer.

quests.title: Live Targets
quests.description:
Drillmaster Hask. Don't stand in the square, that's where things land.

I am running out of recruits who do not mind being hit.

That sounds like a joke and it is a staffing crisis. A drill needs somebody on the receiving end, and the dead are not as indifferent to being struck as the living assume - they're worse, because they've already had the worst thing happen and they've decided that's enough.

So my square is full of recruits who flinch.

Meanwhile the Lordaeron Remnants up in the Ruins are persistent, cheerfully hostile, and entirely unbothered by any of it.

It is high time somebody used them.

North, up the shaft, then south along the road.

Bring back their signets. The recruits learn more off a signet in their hand than off a week of my shouting, and I've had a long time to make peace with that.
quests.accept_text: North up the shaft, south along the road to the Ruins.
quests.turn_in_text:
Good.

The recruits will learn more from these signets than from a month of my yelling, which is both useful and faintly insulting.

quests.title: A Captain for the Pit
quests.description:
Crusader Brennic holds the Scarlet outpost east of Brill.

And I'd like him in the pit. In a manner of speaking - he's not coming to my square and I'm not going to his, so somebody else does the bringing.

Here's my read on the man, for whatever a drillmaster's opinion is worth.

His armour is polished. Properly, daily, by him - I've had that from two scouts and they both noticed independently, which is how you know it's real and not a story.

His faith is brittle.

Those two things go together more often than you'd think. The ones who are certain don't polish anything. The ones who are keeping something at bay put a very great deal of work into the surface.

Break one of them.

I don't much care which. In my experience the other goes with it.
quests.accept_text: The Crusader's Outpost. His armour is polished. His faith is brittle. Break one of them.
quests.turn_in_text: Polished and brittle indeed. Take your prize and tell the recruits you did not enjoy it.

quests.title: Wards of the Old Crypt
quests.description:
Magistrix Valdis. Don't touch the notes, they're ordered in a way that won't survive being helped.

I've been studying the Agamand wards.

And the wards have been studying me. I'd like to say that lightly and I can't - it took me four visits to notice and I've not been able to un-notice it since.

They respond. Not to magic. To attention. I stand in that crypt and read a ward and the next time I come the ward has moved on from the thing I was reading.

So I've stopped going.

What I need instead are grave relics, off the crypt-keepers.

The wights carry them, and so do the graverobbers - which is its own small comedy, because the robbers have been taking exactly the things I want and have no idea what they've got.

The Agamand Family Crypt, Western Tirisfal.

Bring them and I can finish the notes without standing in there again.
quests.accept_text: The Agamand Family Crypt, Western Tirisfal - off the wights and graverobbers.
quests.turn_in_text:
A ward of twelve strokes, carved by a mason who couldn't count.

Delightful. Genuinely - a flawed ward is a ward somebody built by hand, and a hand can be identified.

Thank you.

quests.title: Whose Demon Is It?
quests.description:
Dreadmaster Kol'ven. Sit if you want. Most don't.

I want to know who the Cult of the Damned bargains with.

And before you assume that's professional jealousy - it partly is, and that's not the reason.

The reason is that there are a limited number of things in the dark that will take a bargain, and I know most of them, and I know what each of them charges. If I know who they're dealing with, I know what the Cult has already paid and what it has left to pay with.

That's not theory. That's an inventory.

The cultists carry ledger pages. The pages carry names. The names carry weight, and I mean that literally - some of them are heavier to read than others.

Cult Farm, Eastern Tirisfal. Acolytes and fanatics.

And don't read the last line of any page.

Trust me on that one. I'd rather you simply didn't than understood why.
quests.accept_text: Off the acolytes and fanatics at Cult Farm, Eastern Tirisfal.
quests.turn_in_text:
Six pages.

So it isn't one of mine.

Pity. I'd have enjoyed the argument, and I'd have won it.

quests.title: Venom for the Retorts
quests.description:
Apothecary Marwen. Speak up, and don't stand between me and the bench.

I run on venom, bile and spite. Two of those I'm resupplied with. The third I'm out of.

The Venomweb skitterers east of Brill carry sacs that clear the throat of a retort like nothing else I've found in forty years.

Not a solvent. A solvent takes the residue and it takes the glaze with it, and then your retort is porous and every batch after tastes of the batch before.

These don't. I have no idea why. I have asked three people who should know and received three confident answers that contradicted each other, which is how I knew none of them had tried it.

Sacs, not spiders.

The spiders are mostly legs and I have no use for legs this week.

Venomweb Vale, Eastern Tirisfal. Unbroken - a burst sac is a stain and nothing else.
quests.accept_text: Venomweb Vale, Eastern Tirisfal. Sacs, unbroken.
quests.turn_in_text:
Fat, ripe and unburst.

You have a gift, and I don't say that - most people hand me a bag of wet.

Here. For the effort.

quests.title: A Vial in the Wrong Hands
quests.description:
[A sealed vial, taken off a Plagued Courier on the Silverpine road.]

The Apothecary Society's wax is on the stopper. Unmistakably - the seal's cut deep and the impression is clean, which means it was done at the bench rather than in a hurry.

So this left the Apothecarium properly. Signed out, or near enough.

There's a hairline crack running down one side of the glass.

Fine enough that you'd have to turn it in the light. Not fine enough that the contents are still entirely in there, which is a thought worth having before you put it in a pocket.

[A courier on a forest road with a cracked Society vial is either a theft that went badly or an errand nobody wrote down.]

[The Master Apothecary signs every compound that leaves that lab. She will want to know why one of hers is out in the pines, and she will want to know today.]

objectives.label: Take the stray vial to Master Apothecary Sable

quests.accept_text: The Master Apothecary's lab, in the Apothecarium.
quests.turn_in_text:
The wax is ours.

The compound is not on any ledger I signed.

Someone has been busy behind my back, and they have been busy for long enough to have a courier route.

quests.title: A Scroll for Raven Hill
quests.description:
Loremaster Sennarath. Close the door.

I have tracked the Cult's cipher across half of Lordaeron. Four years of it - farmhouse walls, grave markers, a ledger out of a cult farm, and a line of it in a groundskeeper's pocket that I'm still angry about.

I can read about two thirds.

The missing third is a key, and I've come to believe Keeper Oswin at Raven Hill has it.

Not the whole key. The shape of it - he's been reading the same markings on his own stones for longer than I've been working and he has never once written any of it down, which is either discipline or stubbornness and with Oswin it's both.

This scroll is sealed in grave-wax and it is not leaving this city except in a steady pair of hands.

North, by portal, into Silverpine. Raven Hill Cemetery.

Put it in his hand. And do not read it - not for secrecy. Because the wax only takes one impression and I'll know.

objectives.label: Take the scroll to Keeper Oswin, Raven Hill Cemetery, Silverpine North

quests.accept_text: By portal into Silverpine, to Raven Hill Cemetery. Keeper Oswin.
quests.turn_in_text:
He frowns the way I do. That's a good sign - it means he's reading it rather than deciding about it.

Give me a moment.

There will be a reply. There always is with Oswin and it's always shorter than you'd want.

on_accept.name: Sennarath's Sealed Scroll
on_accept.description: Grave-wax over parchment. It smells of old libraries.

quests.title: Oswin's Reply
quests.description:
[Keeper Oswin has read the scroll twice. He reads everything twice and he has not explained why in thirty years.]

He wrote the reply standing up, at a grave marker, using the stone as a desk.

It is four words long.

[He folds it once, which is not enough folding for anything meant to travel, and hands it over without sealing it.]

She'll know what it means. That's the whole of why it's short - I'd not put more on a road than has to be on a road.

Back to the Undercity. The Magic Quarter.

Keep it dry. Keep it close.

And keep your opinions to yourself, which I say to everyone who carries anything for me and have never once needed to say twice.

objectives.label: Return Oswin's reply to Loremaster Sennarath in the Undercity

quests.accept_text: Back to Loremaster Sennarath, in the Magic Quarter.
quests.turn_in_text:
'Yes, the key is in the husks.'

Of course it is.

Oswin always did like his answers buried. Four years, and he gives me four words, and the maddening thing is that they're enough.

on_accept.name: Oswin's Reply
on_accept.description: Two lines in a cramped hand. The ink is still damp.

quests.title: A Scrap in the Soil
quests.description:
[Torn from the pocket of a Skeletal Groundskeeper at Raven Hill.]

It's a fragment of a ledger, and it is written in the Cult's cipher.

Not copied. Written - the strokes run on and the line ends mid-character where the page tore, which is somebody working at speed in a notation they're fluent in.

[The groundskeeper was not a cultist. It was a groundskeeper, and it was carrying this the way a groundskeeper carries anything: because it was in the pocket when it stopped being alive, and nobody has emptied a pocket at Raven Hill in a very long time.]

[Which means somebody with the cipher was at that cemetery, in person, writing.]

[There is exactly one person in the Undercity who might read it, and she has been chasing this notation for four years.]

objectives.label: Deliver the scrap to Loremaster Sennarath

quests.accept_text: Loremaster Sennarath, in the Magic Quarter.
quests.turn_in_text:
A line of the cipher. In a groundskeeper's pocket.

How very careless of someone.

Thank you. People are careless at the end of a long night, and now I know they had one at Raven Hill.

quests.title: The Pyrewood Pack
quests.description:
Ranger Isolde. Walk with me - I don't brief standing still, it's a bad habit to teach anyone.

I hunt what the Dark Lady needs hunted. That's the post and it's as much latitude as it sounds.

This season it's the worgen around Pyrewood.

Three things have changed and only the third one worries me.

They're thickening in number. Ordinary - a good year for something is a good year.

They're bolder in daylight. Less ordinary, and it usually means hunger.

And the ambushers have started working the treeline rather than the road.

That's the one. An ambusher on a road is waiting for traffic. An ambusher on a treeline is waiting for whoever comes to deal with the ones on the road.

So they've started planning for us.

Pyrewood Village, Silverpine South. Ambushers and the feral ones both.

Watch the treeline. They love the treeline and now you know why.
quests.accept_text: Pyrewood Village, Silverpine South. Watch the treeline.
quests.turn_in_text:
Twelve fewer to watch.

The Dark Lady will hear of it - if only because I'll tell her, which is most of how she hears anything.

quests.title: The Watchman Who Stayed
quests.description:
Deathstalker Rhyne. I'll be brief; I've been asked to do this quietly and talking isn't quiet.

There's a Forsaken Watchman at Raven Hill who never stopped his patrol.

One of ours. That's the whole of the problem and the reason this came to me rather than to a ranger.

He doesn't answer challenges. He doesn't answer his own name - I went up there myself and used it, twice, at ten paces, and got nothing.

And he's still walking the route. Correctly. The same beat he was given, at the right hours, with the right turns at the right stones.

So there's enough left to keep the post and nothing left to be relieved of it.

I've been asked to put him down quietly.

I've decided the quiet option is you.

The groundskeepers first - they hear everything, and they'll bring him to you if you don't. Then him.
quests.accept_text: Raven Hill Cemetery, Silverpine North. Groundskeepers first.
quests.turn_in_text:
Quiet work. Efficient.

I may recommend you to Rhyne's less dignified cousins, and I'd take that as a compliment if I were you, because nobody else would.

quests.title: The Dark Lady's Ear
quests.description:
Stand still a moment. This is not a task and I'd rather you weren't surprised by it.

Three separate reports have reached me, from three people who do not speak to each other.

The Scarlet interrogator's ledger. The necromancer in the Scourge Cave. And the Agamand cipher out of Silverpine.

Each one is a thread. On its own, each one is a local problem with a local explanation, and that is how all three were filed by the people who sent them.

They are the same thread.

I have been in this office long enough to know what it costs to say that out loud, and I'm saying it.

Sylvanas would like to see them tied.

And whoever carried all three ought to be the one standing in front of her, rather than me reading them out and taking the credit, which I considered for about an afternoon.

The great hall, Royal Quarter.

Bow, if the knees allow it. Mine don't.
quests.accept_text: The great hall of the Royal Quarter. Stand before the Dark Lady.
quests.turn_in_text:
She has been told.

She says: 'Remember the face.'

I would take that as the highest praise she gives. I have heard her give it twice.

quests.title: The Seal at the Bottom
quests.description:
Gatewarden Sorrel. Keep your voice down near the door - not for them. For me.

I keep the iron door at the south end of the wheel.

Nothing has come up from the Deeps for weeks.

And everybody I've told has congratulated me, which is how I know none of them have held this post.

Something always comes up. That's the arrangement and it's been the arrangement since I was given this door - things come up, I put them back down, I write the number in a book. The book is the job.

My book has been empty for six weeks.

A quiet door is not a safe door. A quiet door is a door where something has stopped sending the small things, and the only reason to stop sending the small things is that you're organising the large ones.

Stand at it. Count to thirty. Tell me if you hear anything.

And do not open it. I want that said in the plainest words I've got.
quests.accept_text: The iron door at the south end of the wheel. Count to thirty. Don't open it.
quests.turn_in_text:
You heard it too, then.

Good. I had started to wonder about myself, and a gatewarden who wonders about herself is no use to anybody.

Come back when you are much stronger. There is work below and it will not be small.

quests.title: Cull the Cistern
quests.description:
You came back. And you came back stronger, which is what I asked for and not what I expected.

I am no longer certain what is coming up that stair.

That's a change and it's the worst kind. For years I could name everything that came through this door - rats, worms, the occasional thing a lab had finished with. I knew the inventory.

Now the Outer Cistern is flooding with zombies, hounds and rot worms, and they are not the ones I know.

Whatever the Society's alchemists are breeding down there has got away from them. Or hasn't, and is being released, and I've stopped being able to tell which of those I'd prefer.

I want the first chamber quieter.

Not cleared. Quieter - enough that somebody can stand in it and look at what the rest of it is doing.

Through the iron door, then down.

Bring friends. The Society's work is not for lone travellers and it was never designed to be.
quests.accept_text: Through the iron door and down, into the Outer Cistern.
quests.turn_in_text:
You came up with all your limbs and a better colour than most.

That is progress. I'd not have called it that a month ago and I'm calling it that now.

quests.title: Sump Samples
quests.description:
Master Apothecary Lorrane Sable. Shut the door behind you. I'll explain why in a moment and you won't like it.

I cannot prove this yet, which is why you're hearing it in a closed room.

I believe the sump water in the Plague Depths is carrying the plague into the Cistern's lower works.

Not leaking. Carrying - as a medium, deliberately, the way a solvent carries a compound where you want it to go.

And the reason that matters is the direction. Waste goes down. Everything about that cistern was built on the assumption that waste goes down.

Something down there is running it the other way.

I want sealed vials of the sludge. Off the spore-things and the rot worms both - they're saturated with it and they're easier to take samples off than a sump.

Stoppers on. Properly on.

And if you drop one, don't tell me. I have enough to be going on with.
quests.accept_text: The Outer Cistern. Plague Spores and Rot Worms. Six vials, stoppers on. If you drop one, don't tell me.
quests.turn_in_text: Six. Green-grey. Warm. Not natural, not remotely. Someone is feeding this on purpose. Thank you.

quests.title: The Plagueweaver
quests.description:
[She has the samples laid out in a row and she does not look up for a while.]

The sludge reads like a recipe.

That's not a figure of speech. There's a sequence in it - a base, a binder, and then a flourish at the end that does nothing a chemist would ask for and everything a craftsman would.

I know the hand.

It's Vex's. Plagueweaver of the Society's inner circle, and she weaves the plague through the Weaving Hall's looms.

I trained alongside her. Forty years. She is the only person I have ever let read my notes before they were finished.

And she is not working for the Dark Lady any more. That is not an accusation I make lightly and it is not an accusation at this point, it is a reading off a vial.

The Weaving Hall, west of the Mid Conduit.

She was a friend once.

That is the worst of it, and I'd rather have said so than have you find out from someone else afterward.
quests.accept_text: The Weaving Hall, west of the Mid Conduit.
quests.turn_in_text:
Her needle. Of course it was the needle.

She always did sew too tightly. I told her so for forty years and she took it as a compliment every time.

Thank you. And I am sorry you had to be the one.

quests.title: The Surgeon's Notes
quests.description:
Marwen again. Something less pleasant than venom sacs.

I've heard the Plague Surgeons down there are the Society's loyal hands.

Loyal, mind - not conspirators. There's a distinction and it's the entire reason I want their papers.

A conspirator destroys his notes. A loyal man keeps them, because he has never once imagined being asked to explain himself.

And they are taking notes. A clinical record of the plague's progress - rate, spread, what it does and in what order.

If there's a ledger of the spread anywhere in this city, it is in those surgeons' coats.

I want it. Not to prosecute anybody - I leave that to Sable and she's welcome to it.

I want to know how it moves, because nobody in this city actually does, and we have all been pretending otherwise for three years.

The Lab wing. The pages are bloodied but legible.
quests.accept_text: Off the Plague Surgeons in the Lab wing.
quests.turn_in_text:
A neat hand. A steady one.

And a growing unease in the last entries - the writing gets smaller toward the end, which is what a man does when he's stopped wanting the page to be read.

We know how it spreads now. That's the first true thing anyone's said about it.

quests.title: The Court's Ledger
quests.description:
Sennarath. I've moved from ciphers to accounting, which I'd have found humiliating a year ago.

I know who the conspirators bribed.

Or rather - I know that it is knowable, which is a different and better thing, and here is why.

The Blighted Courtiers of the Throne of Rot keep a ledger of every favour.

Every one. Given, received, owed, settled. It is the single most meticulous document I have ever heard described and it is being kept by things that cannot leave a room.

That is what court does to people. They kept a ledger alive, they kept it after they died, and not one of them has ever thought to stop.

I want copies. Any condition - I can read through a stain and I have had a great deal of practice.

The Court of Rot, north-west wing.

Four will do. I'll set them against Wrenfall's lists and we'll see whose names appear on both.
quests.accept_text: The Court of Rot, north-west wing. The Blighted Courtiers. Four ledgers, any condition. I can read through a stain.
quests.turn_in_text: Names, dates, sums. Every one struck through, and every sum still correct. Terrifying and tidy. Thank you.

quests.title: The Infected Noble
quests.description:
Wrenfall. This one is distasteful and I'll not dress it.

The Faulkner line was Lordaeron nobility. Old, undistinguished, and entirely legitimate, which is the only part that matters here.

The last Faulkner was murdered in his bed.

Then raised in a vat. Then given a signet he does not remember ever owning.

The Society dressed him as a figurehead for the coup, and they chose well - a real name, a real line, and a man with no memory of either to contradict anybody about it.

He is not guilty of anything. I want that on the record once, because I am about to ask you to kill him and I would rather do that honestly.

He is also the legitimacy the whole conspiracy rests on.

Throne of Rot, the west wing.

Take the signet off the body.

And do not wear it. Not as a joke, not to see. Two people have, and I had to deal with both.
quests.accept_text: Throne of Rot, the Plague Depths' west wing. Kill him. Take the signet off the body. Do not wear it.
quests.turn_in_text: A dead man's ring on a dead man's finger. Good. It goes in the vault, and the vault stays shut.

quests.title: Voss's Codex
quests.description:
Plague Keeper Voss keeps the Archive, and I want the Archive more than I want Voss.

A thousand recipes. A thousand formulae. And - this is the part nobody else has grasped - the notes that tie them together.

Anybody can steal a recipe. A recipe on its own is a dead thing; you can hold one for years and never work out what it was for.

The Codex is the index.

It says which formula was made for which purpose on which date, and once you have that you can read the whole conspiracy's intentions backward out of its own stores.

I want it in one piece.

That matters more than speed and more than Voss. A Codex with pages missing is a Codex that will mislead me confidently for a year.

The Blight Archive, east wing.

Voss is a careful curator - he will try to destroy it before he loses it, because that is what a careful curator does.

Be more careful than he is.
quests.accept_text: The Blight Archive, east wing. Voss is a careful curator. Be more careful.
quests.turn_in_text: A thousand recipes, one ledger. The conspiracy is on every page. We may yet outpace it.

quests.title: Vat-Born Tissue
quests.description:
Surgeon Halvard. Gloves - take a pair, I'm not asking.

I need to see what the Society has been growing in the Vault of Flesh.

And I need it from tissue rather than from a report, because a report tells me what somebody decided to write down and tissue tells me how long.

That's the actual question. Not what they're growing. How long they've been doing it.

There's an answer in the material itself - the way it's layered, what it's tried to become and given up on - and I can read that the way you'd read rings in a felled tree.

The failed experiments carry fistfuls of it. Still working out what they were supposed to be, which is the phrase I've settled on and I'm aware of how it sounds.

The Vault of Flesh, east wing.

Gloves on.

And don't think about the faces. That's not squeamishness - the ones who think about the faces come back with nothing usable.
quests.accept_text: The Vault of Flesh, east wing. Failed Experiments. Gloves on. Don't think about the faces.
quests.turn_in_text: Five. Fresh, grey and still trying. The vats have been running longer than anyone told me.

quests.title: What the Vats Grew
quests.description:
The samples point one direction and I'd hoped they wouldn't.

They're not from the vats. They're from something IN the vats - a single source at the heart of the Vault, and everything you brought me is a failed attempt at being it.

It's still growing.

That's what the layering says and I've checked it four times because I wanted to be wrong. There's no outer limit written into it. Whatever was supposed to tell the thing when to stop was never put in, or was taken out.

I call it the Vile Plague Abomination, which is not a clinical name and I've stopped pretending I want one.

It does not recognise anything as a friend.

I want that understood rather than assumed - it's not hostile, it has no category for you. The Society's own people go into that chamber and do not come out, and I have the tissue to prove at least two of them did.

Deepest chamber of the Vault.

It is large, loud and wet. Bring a healer.
quests.accept_text: The Vault of Flesh, deepest chamber. It is large, loud and wet. Bring a healer.
quests.turn_in_text: Growth stopped. Marvellous and terrible. The Society should be ashamed. Take the pick of what's left.

quests.title: The Heart of the Plague
quests.description:
Sit. This is the last of it and I want to say it in order.

Vex. The Noble. Voss. The Abomination.

Four limbs. I've been treating them as four conspiracies for a month and they were never that - a weaver, a figurehead, an archive and a weapon, which is exactly the four things a coup needs and nothing it doesn't.

Zul'keth is the heart.

A Dark Sorcerer who believes the Dark Lady has failed. Not betrayed us - FAILED, and that distinction is why he's dangerous. A traitor can be bargained with. A man who thinks he is correcting an error cannot.

And he has built a pulsing furnace of plague under this city to prove it.

Under it. While we all walked the wheel and filed reports and congratulated a gatewarden on a quiet door.

The Plague Heart. The deepest room.

Everything you've killed down there was his.

Finish it.
quests.accept_text: The Plague Heart, the deepest room. Everything you've killed so far was his. Finish it.
quests.turn_in_text: It beats no more. The Society is leaderless and the Dark Lady is still on her throne. Take her gratitude, and mine.

on_turn_in.name: Sable's Sealed Report
on_turn_in.description: Four pages and a seal. The conspiracy in full, signed off by the one person who could.

quests.title: The Dark Lady's Gratitude
quests.description:
It's written. The whole sorry tale, sealed, and I've read it back twice and hated it both times.

It needs to reach the Queen.

Not by messenger. Not by raven, and not by me - and I'd like to explain that last one properly rather than let you think it's modesty.

I signed the wax on the vial that started this. My seal was on the thing that was being carried through Silverpine by a courier I did not send. Whatever this report says about the Society, it says about my office, and a report like that should not arrive in the hand of the person it implicates.

It should arrive in the hand that finished it.

The Royal Quarter's great hall.

Hand it to her.

And do not say anything clever. I have watched three people say something clever in that hall and I have seen what she does with her face while they do it.

objectives.label: Take Sable's report to Lady Sylvanas

quests.accept_text: The Royal Quarter's great hall. Hand it to her. Do not say anything clever.
quests.turn_in_text: She reads it, slowly. She says nothing. Then she says: 'The Forsaken do not forget.' That is as close to thanks as the Dark Lady gets.

quests.title: A Writ for the Frontier
quests.description: The Undercity signs writs and the frontier receives them, usually late and usually about something the frontier has already dealt with. This one is different: it is a standing authority for the commander at Tarren Mill to act in the valley without referring north, and the Executor has had it sitting on his desk for a month because signing it means admitting he cannot run Hillsbrad from here.

objectives.label: Deliver the writ to Commander Vellis Thorne in Tarren Mill

quests.accept_text:
South. Through Silverpine, down into Hillsbrad, east to a mill town cut in half by a water channel. Thorne holds it.

The writ gives her authority I would rather keep. I am sending it anyway, because the alternative is losing the valley by post.
quests.turn_in_text:
He signed it.

I have been asking for this for two years and I had stopped expecting it. Do you know what this is? It is permission to stop waiting.

There is Alterac money in these hills, there are wizards in a scrap camp, and there is a man in Durnholde keeping a court. I can go after all three now without writing north first.

on_accept.name: Royal Writ of the Frontier
on_accept.description: A standing authority for the Tarren Mill garrison to act in Hillsbrad without referring to the Undercity. Sealed, and heavier than paper should be.
